title: Security posture discovery with Sierra Pharma
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 summary
Share Private deployment network diagram + VPC onboarding checklist
Schedule SE-led demo for Private deployment with Derek and Priya (week of 2027-01-25)
Provide Dedicated vs Private pricing sheet and expected SLA commitments
action_items: Samir: Email SOC2 + ISO docs by 2027-01-17
Alex: Prepare VPC peering and egress rules doc by 2027-01-19
Priya: Share their data retention policy and sample retention windows by 2027-01-20
summary: Intro discovery focused on Sierra Pharma's security posture and whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private fits their regulatory needs. Main concerns: SOC2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, KMS integration and BYOK, data residency and retention. Next steps agreed: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, network onboarding docs, schedule deeper Private deployment demo.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account, with me is Alex Chen from our security and infra team. How are you folks?
[00:08] Maya Lawson: Good thanks, Maya here. CISO at Sierra Pharma, joining Derek and Priya. We set aside 45 mins to run through security posture questions

- SOC2, SAML, encryption, that sort of stuff.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Perfect. High level, do you want to kick off with your top compliance asks?
[00:22] Maya Lawson: Sure. We're regulated

- need SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, ISO27001 is a big plus. Also must support SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning, RBAC so we can map roles to our internal groups, and detailed audit logs for e-discovery. Data residency and retention windows are important for our clinical trial data too.
[00:38] Alex Chen: Totally expected. Quick overview: Redwood offers Hosted (our multi-tenant API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation), and Private (VPC or on-prem bundle). For SOC2 and ISO we can share our Type II report and ISO summary; Dedicated and Private are common for customers with strict data isolation and VPC requirements.
[00:54] Derek Cole: When you say Dedicated, is data still leaving our VPC? How does network flow work?
[00:58] Alex Chen: Good question. Dedicated is still in our cloud but we isolate compute on dedicated pools and we support VPC peering or private link for egress. Traffic between your app and our endpoints is TLS. With Private deployment we can either deploy a control plane in Redwood and nodes in your VPC, or do an on-prem bundle, which gives you full network control.
[01:14] Priya Nair: For encryption: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM? We need to ensure keys are under our control for certain datasets.
[01:20] Alex Chen: Yes, we support KMS integrations. For Hosted we offer our managed KMS by default but can enable BYOK for Dedicated and Private. For Private deployments you can integrate your KMS or HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM). There are a few operational notes around cache eviction and key rotation we can share.
[01:34] Maya Lawson: Audit logs

- what granularity, and how long do you retain them by default? We may need 2+ years for certain investigations.
[01:41] Samir Patel: Our Console produces per-request audit trails: request metadata, model used, tokens consumed, principals, and routing decisions. Default retention for Hosted is 90 days, but for Enterprise we offer configurable retention windows; Dedicated can extend retention, and Private leaves retention to your policy. We can export logs to your SIEM (S3, CloudWatch, Splunk) and set up long-term archival.
[01:58] Derek Cole: Is there PII in logs

- do you redact payloads by default?
[02:02] Alex Chen: Payload logging is opt-in. For Hosted, we redact at rest unless you opt into request logging. For Dedicated/Private we support redaction policies and endpoint-level controls. We also support prefix/KV cache controls so sensitive prefixes can be excluded from cache and logs.
[02:16] Maya Lawson: SSO and provisioning

- SAML ok but we prefer SCIM for group sync. What's your experience?
[02:21] Samir Patel: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO plus SCIM for user and group provisioning. For Hosted customers we run the IdP integrations through our SaaS control plane; for Private deployments you can run the SCIM endpoint inside your network. We also support RBAC with custom roles and resource-level permissions.
[02:36] Priya Nair: For RBAC do you have least-privilege templates? We need role separation between operators, model owners, and auditors.
[02:41] Alex Chen: Yes. We have built-in roles (Admin, Operator, Auditor, Developer) and you can create custom roles. Policies are ABAC-like with resource tags; we can map to Okta groups or your IdP groups via SCIM. We'll share our role matrix.
[02:55] Maya Lawson: Do you have SOC2 Type II report we can review? And do you support third-party audits?
[03:00] Samir Patel: Yes

- we'll send the SOC2 Type II report and an ISO27001 conformance summary. We regularly undergo third-party audits and can provide an attestations pack. Link to docs: https://redwood.example/security (we'll send the specific pdfs).
[03:11] Derek Cole: For private deployment, what does onboarding look like? How long before it's production ready?
[03:16] Alex Chen: Typical Private onboard is 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM provisioning. Dedicated can be quicker

- 2-4 weeks. Hosted is immediate but comes with default retention and managed KMS unless you request BYOK. We'll attach a network checklist that outlines firewall rules, egress IPs, DNS, and ILB requirements.
[03:33] Priya Nair: Any particular compliance caveats around model weights or caching

- like do you ever persist user prompts outside customer control?
[03:39] Alex Chen: For Hosted some telemetry and anonymized usage is kept for platform metrics, but customer data persists only per your retention policy. We offer a no-persist mode for sensitive workloads

- requests aren't stored beyond ephemeral processing

- and Dedicated/Private gives you full control over persistent storage.
[03:54] Maya Lawson: Can you speak to incident response and breach notifications? SLA around notification windows?
[03:59] Samir Patel: We have a documented incident response plan and SOC/Legal notifications. For Enterprise customers we provide 24/7 pager escalation and committed notification windows in our contract (we can include in the SLA). We'll include an excerpt in the docs we send.
[04:11] Derek Cole: Do you support VPC endpoints/private link for lower attack surface?
[04:15] Alex Chen: Yes

- PrivateLink and VPC peering supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have IP allowlisting and TLS enforced.
[04:23] Maya Lawson: Any penalties or contractual language around subprocessor usage or cross-border data transfer? We need clarity for EU data flows.
[04:30] Samir Patel: We provide a standard data processing agreement, and we have EU region options. For Private deployments you can keep data in-region. For Hosted/Dedicated, we can sign EU addendums and restrict model routing to EU regions for data residency.
[04:44] Priya Nair: For demo

- can you show a Private deployment architecture and how KMS/BYOK integrates?
[04:49] Alex Chen: Absolutely

- we'll schedule a deeper SE-led session. Suggested participants: Derek, Priya, and Maya. Week of Jan 25 works?
[04:56] Maya Lawson: That works for us.
[04:58] Samir Patel: Great. Quick recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, provide VPC/net onboarding checklist, share RBAC role matrix, and schedule the SE demo. Any blockers?
[05:08] Maya Lawson: Nothing else on our side

- we'll review docs and circle back.
[05:11] Samir Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for the demo.
[05:15] [call ends]
